CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding with fatigue and dizziness.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie is a 49-year-old female presenting for evaluation of low hemoglobin. She reports experiencing fatigue and dizziness over the past couple of months. She notes that activities she previously performed daily without difficulty, such as walking a mile or going to work, now leave her worn out and tired. She denies blood in stools, dark or tarry stools, heavy menstrual bleeding, weight loss, loss of appetite, syncope, or severe dizziness. She reports mild leg swelling which she attributes to increased salt intake while traveling. She denies shortness of breath or orthopnea. She has had no recent flank or back pain or hematuria related to her history of kidney stones.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
She reports seasonal nasal congestion related to seasonal allergies. She denies fever, chills, sore throat, or cough. All other systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, kidney stones, and prior colonoscopy with findings of mild diverticulosis three years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Toprol 50 milligrams daily, lisinopril 10 milligrams daily.

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports recent travel to Vermont. She acknowledges dietary indiscretion including fast food consumption and difficulty with salt restriction.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure and heart rate within normal limits. Cardiac exam: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard. Extremities: Trace to 1+ pitting edema in bilateral ankles. Otherwise unremarkable.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from six months ago shows ejection fraction of 45% with moderate mitral regurgitation. Hemoglobin: 8.2 (low).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. New anemia: Order anemia profile labs to determine etiology. Refer to gastroenterology for endoscopy and colonoscopy evaluation.
2. Congestive heart failure: Start lasix 40 milligrams once daily for fluid retention. Continue toprol 50 milligrams daily and lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Strict salt restriction advised. Patient to weigh herself daily and call if weight increases. May require additional diuretic adjustment.
3. Kidney stones: No acute issues at this time. Continue dietary awareness and hydration, recognizing diuretic use may complicate this. Follow up as needed.
